audit_findings.title: Convertible-note treatment mixes debt and equity claims
audit_findings.magnitude: $420.0m cash-settled principal; 7.942578m underlying shares included; at least 4.960m principal-equivalent shares are excess, with up to 7.943m excess after capped-call protection
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator includes shares for the entire note conversion value although principal is cash-settled; OE retains note interest, and capped calls offset conversion-spread dilution up to $86.174.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company will settle conversions by paying cash up to the outstanding principal amount, and at the Company’s election, will settle the conversion spread by paying or delivering cash or shares of its common stock, or a combination of cash and shares of its common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated internal inconsistency. The included note shares equal 14.3% of the 55.408m denominator. Removing only the principal-equivalent portion raises base value from $61.59 to approximately $67.65 per share; removing all note shares raises it to approximately $71.91. That is large enough to alter the assessed valuation range and margin-of-safety threshold, even though the corrected base case remains below the $84.68 market price.
audit_findings.action: Rerun all scenarios using cash-settled principal, expected conversion-spread dilution at $84.68, and an explicit capped-call offset; alternatively, model full conversion with matching numerator, interest, debt, cash, and capped-call adjustments.

audit_findings.title: Long-term marketable securities appear omitted after investment income was purged
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonoperating bridge adds cash and short-term securities but omits long-term debt securities whose interest income was removed from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The short-term and long-term portions were $ 203.6 million and $ 76.2 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated by the $958.0m bridge equaling approximately $754.5m of cash plus $203.5m of current marketable securities. Adding $76.2m would raise base value from $61.59 to about $62.97 per share, only 2.2%, and would leave it well below the $84.68 market price and the valuation conclusion unchanged.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the portfolio was unrestricted and nonoperating, determine its net realizable value and any tax or disposition costs, and add that amount to the bridge in the corrected rerun.

audit_findings.title: Publicly traded equity investments are absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $42.3m omitted asset, approximately $0.76 per diluted share; $24.0m filed FY2026 unrealized loss with exact OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge may omit a nonoperating equity asset, while any unrealized or realized investment result left in OE would inconsistently affect the earnings anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company’s investments in publicly held equity securities were $ 42.3 million and $ 19.9 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The missing $42.3m asset alone would increase base value only about 1.2% and would not change the conclusion. However, the filing also reports a $24.0m unrealized loss, equal to 13.7% of the $174.7m anchor before considering taxes. The supplied record does not establish whether that loss was purged from OE, so a potentially larger normalization error remains unresolved and its materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $42.3m securities into the bridge and reconcile every realized and unrealized equity-investment item to the FY2026 OE calculation; then rerun the bridge and anchor if either was omitted or retained inconsistently.

audit_findings.title: Nonvested restricted shares may be counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: 0.401198m shares, 0.72% of the denominator; approximately $0.45 per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: Issued restricted shares are already included in reported common shares outstanding but appear to have been added again to fully diluted shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Common stock outstanding reflected in the Company’s consolidated balance sheets includes restricted stock awards outstanding.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing expressly states that balance-sheet common shares outstanding include restricted stock awards, making the duplication a demonstrated error if the valuation added all 0.401198m nonvested shares. Removing them would raise base value from $61.59 to approximately $62.04, less than 1%, and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $84.68 price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the July 31 cover count to the restricted-stock ledger and remove the 0.401198m shares to the extent they are already legally outstanding.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 contains a nonrecurring lease-termination gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.3m pre-tax, equal to 8.2% of the $174.7m anchor; exact OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the one-time gain increases the FY2026 OE anchor and every forecast cash flow derived from it; related noncash lease-asset and liability adjustments could offset it in a cash-flow-based calculation.
audit_findings.evidence: In December 2025, the Company signed an agreement with the landlord of its San Francisco lease to terminate the lease prior its expiration date and recorded a lease termination gain of $ 14.3 million as a result of eliminating its remaining lease liability and right-of-use asset.
audit_findings.explanation: The $14.3m gain is filed and nonrecurring, but the record does not show whether it survived the OE reconciliation. Because the cash-flow statement contains aggregated noncash and lease-liability adjustments, neither the existence nor the after-tax size of a valuation error is demonstrated. Its possible scale warrants resolution, but materiality cannot be established from the supplied calculation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile net income through operating cash flow and OE line by line, identifying the gain, right-of-use-asset removal, lease-liability removal, tax effect, and any cash termination payment; rerun only if a net benefit remains in OE.

audit_findings.title: Vested but unsettled DSUs may be missing from the denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Vested DSUs remain common-equity claims until director separation and share issuance, so omitted units would understate fully diluted shares and overstate per-share value.
audit_findings.evidence: The DSUs vest on the grant-date anniversary and are settled in the form of shares of common stock issued to the holder upon separation from the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that DSUs settle only upon separation and reports 81,103 nonvested units, but it does not disclose the total vested-but-unsettled ledger. Prior-year vesting activity does not establish how many units remained unsettled at the valuation date. The possible omission is therefore unresolved, and the record cannot support either its count or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the complete director DSU ledger as of the valuation date, reconcile vested units to issued shares and the cover count, add only vested-but-unsettled claims, and rerun per-share values.
